Subject: Data disposition window and subprocessor sequencing

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is trying to reconcile the DPA retention language with our internal disposition requirements and we need to understand how Redwood will sequence the actual purges across live stores, backups, and log archives. A few questions from our side:

- If a user requests deletion (DAS request), what is the end-to-end timeline until data is removed from:
  * primary store,
  * immutable backup snapshots, and
  * long-term logs (audit/tracing)?
- Do you provide a way to schedule a coordinated purge across subprocessors so we can control the customer-facing disposition effective date?
- Are there rollback/restore windows after a purge is triggered (for accidental deletions)? If so, how long and what triggers are required?

We also need to know whether Redwood can sign a narrow amendment to the DPA to add a 90-day disposition hold in case of litigation or regulatory review, and how that would affect backup purges. Attached: subproc_matrix_v2.xlsx with our current subprocessor list.

Procurement has a target go-live for May 1, so we need concrete behavior and timelines this quarter. Please loop in your security/trust lead for any exception process.

Thanks,
Diana Lopez
Data Privacy Program Manager
MedSys Health

Attachments: subproc_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Hi Diana — appreciate the detail and the matrix. Looping in Kim and Laura to confirm ops and legal constraints. High-level answers below; we can follow with a short call to lock dates.

Summary proposal (high level):
- Primary store: deletion is applied within 24 hours of an approved DAS request; object references are tombstoned immediately and blobs are scheduled for secure deletion.
- Immutable snapshots/backups: controlled by snapshot retention policy. We recommend a staggered approach: snapshot expiry set to 30 days after the disposition effective date by default, with the ability to request a temporary hold (up to 90 days) scoped to account/deal via DPA amendment.
- Logs/audit traces: default retention 180 days. For customers who need shorter retention we can apply a carveout; for longer retention we handle exceptions via audit ticket and a documented exception workflow.
- Emergency rollback: we offer a 14-day rollback window from snapshot expiry when the escrowed snapshot is still present. Restores after that require special legal procurement and may be possible depending on overwrite/garbage collection.

Operationally: we can provide a subprocessor purge calendar (who purges and when) and will accept mutually agreed handoff dates. When you request a disposition effective date, we coordinate a purge window across Redwood and listed subprocessors in the matrix.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly to propose a purge calendar and the exception request flow (ticket + approvers).
2) Laura to confirm DPA amendment language and whether we can append a 90-day limited hold clause for regulated reviews.
3) 30-min call next week to agree timelines.

I've attached a draft timeline (proposed-disposition-timeline.pdf). If this aligns we'll push a formal amendment and a short SOW for purge coordination.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-disposition-timeline.pdf (PDF)

Hi Diana — thanks for the clear asks. Below is the operational purge calendar and attestation workflow we propose. This is scoped to the subprocessor matrix you shared; if new subprocessors are added we'll update the calendar.

Proposed purge calendar (account-level coordination):
- Day 0 (Disposition effective date): primary store tombstone applied within 24 hours.
- Day 1–7: queued snapshot markers created; backup snapshots flagged for purge.
- Day 30: scheduled snapshot expiry and secure overwrite kick-off for short-term backups.
- Day 30–44: subprocessor purge windows — each subprocessor receives a 14-day window in which to execute purges; they must confirm completion in the audit ticket.
- Day 30–104: optional DPA amendment hold window (up to 90 days) if legal/regulatory hold is invoked — during this window purges are paused.
- Day 180: default logs/audit traces are removed unless an exception ticket is open.

Attestation and evidence:
- Subprocessors must post a signed deletion confirmation to our secure evidence bucket. Each confirmation includes: subprocessor name, timestamp (UTC), file-key hashes (SHA256), and a signed statement of scope.
- Redwood will relay confirmations to the customer and store hashes in the audit log for 7 years. Evidence links will be included in the audit ticket.

Key management and cross-border notes:
- We support customer-managed keys (CMK) via our KMS integration; if CMK is enabled, Redwood cannot decrypt backups without key access. For cross-border purges requiring Redwood or a subprocessor to access objects encrypted with CMK, the customer must provide a scoped key or explicit concurrence in the amendment.

Rollback and restore process:
- The 14-day rollback window is a manual ops process for restores from flagged snapshots; customers can request an expedited self-serve API restore only if the snapshot has not yet been overwritten. We will document the SLAs in the runbook (target: 24–48 hours for restore by ops).

Next operational items we will deliver by EOD Wednesday:
1) A populated purge calendar with named subprocessor contacts and tentative dates (we will confirm within 48 hours).
2) A sample signed deletion confirmation template.
3) A short audit-ticket runbook describing exception approvals and evidence flow.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call once you confirm the proposed windows.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
